_meta.name: garda-rr-v1
_meta.label: Garda R:R v1 — tail suppression + fee-hold
_meta.description: Risk:reward redesign for Meridian Solana. Thesis: the negative expectancy is NOT the TP/SL band (TP fired 4x and SL 3x in 162 closes = 4.3% of exits). It is 7 tail losses (4.3% of trades) summing -255% while the other 155 trades sum +40% (ex-tail mean +0.259%/trade). So: suppress tails (entry gates + tighter PnL breakers), and shift the exit mix from zero-fee churn toward the two exit classes that actually make money (TRAILING_TP ex-tail +2.32%, CHART_EXIT +0.55%). Ships dryRun=true — evaluation phase, not live.
_meta.source: Audit of lessons.json performance (n=162 closes, 2026-07-02..07-18) + state.json closedOutcomes (n=19) by Claude, 2026-07-26. Handoff: /root/shared-telegram/HANDOFF_CLAUDE_MERIDIAN_RR_V1.md (job meridian-rr-v1-a1). Corroborates the independent 154-trade audit in notes/HANDOFF.md (2026-07-17).
notes: EVALUATION PRESET — dryRun is forced true in overrides and deliberately NOT in the preserve list (compounding.draft preserved dryRun, which is why live config sat at dryRun=false with a 0 SOL wallet). Owner must flip dryRun manually after reviewing dry-run cycles.

Position size is UNCHANGED on purpose: deployAmountSol 0.5, maxDeployAmount 0.5, maxPositions 1. The handoff forbids raising size. Do not 'scale up because it looks better' before real dry-run evidence.

takeProfitPct 4 -> 7. Counter-intuitive but data-driven: TAKE_PROFIT fired only 4/162 times because trailing (arms at +2%) harvests winners first. Holds >=90min have median +3.68% / ex-tail mean +2.78%, so the 4% cap was clipping the only bucket that pays. TP now acts as a spike cap, not the primary harvest.

trailingTriggerPct KEPT at 2 — this is a deliberate DEVIATION from the handoff's suggested 3. TRAILING_TP is the single best exit class (n=9, mean +2.32%, 78% win rate, 85min avg hold, $0.69 avg fees = ~46x the book average). Arming early is what creates that class; with a median trade of ~0.00% a trigger of 3 would disarm it.
trailingDropPct 1 -> 1.5 to let runners breathe, since the >=90min bucket shows we were cutting winners early. Costs ~0.5% extra giveback per trailing exit.

stopLossPct -8 -> -6 and maxLossPct -12 -> -9. Median absolute move is ~0.01%, so -6% is ~600x typical noise and will not fire on bin oscillation. The two SL fires in history closed at -12.28% and -9.50% under an older -20% SL, i.e. the emergency backstop was doing the stop's job. maxLossPct stays ~1.5x SL so rule 0 only matters if rule 1 is bypassed.
minAgeBeforeTakeProfit 10 -> 15: the <15min hold bucket is the worst (mean -2.44%) and first-tick PnL is unreliable (see pnl_pct_suspicious). Don't book phantom profit.
outOfRangeWaitMinutes 10 -> 15: OOR is the ONLY exit class negative ex-tail (-0.070%) with essentially zero fees ($0.004 avg). 24% win rate over 25 closes. Give price a chance to re-enter.

rebalanceMinOorMinutes 20 -> 10 so a rebalance is ATTEMPTED before the 15min OOR close. Previously rebalance (20m) could never fire ahead of the OOR close (10m) — it was dead config. This is the one genuine hypothesis knob in this preset: it converts churn-losses into continued fee earning, but the rebalance path has a known failure mode ('rebalance failed after withdraw'). WATCH THIS in dry-run.

BIN CONCENTRATION is the biggest fee lever found: bins_below <70 -> ex-tail +0.652%/trade and $0.488 avg fees; 70-140 -> +0.244% / $0.097; >140 -> +0.131% / $0.014 (35x less fee capture). So maxBinsBelow + autoStrategyMaxBins 166 -> 140 and defaultBinsBelow 110 -> 90. minBinsBelow stays 70 as the downside-safety floor per handoff (floor MIN_SAFE_BINS_BELOW=35 in config.js).

strategy base bid_ask -> spot. 91 of 162 closes had bins_above=0 (49% of those exited via OOR/pumped-above, $0.013 avg fees, mean -1.63%); bins_above>30 exited OOR only 2% of the time with 12x the fees and +0.357% ex-tail. Per notes/HANDOFF.md a single-sided SOL bid_ask is HARD-CONSTRAINED by the SDK to bins_above=0 (deploy.js throws otherwise), so spot is the only config lever that buys upside cover. autoStrategy stays ON and can still route to bid_ask/curve.
spot carries a higher tail RATE than bid_ask (3/29 = 10.3% vs 4/129 = 3.1%), which is exactly why the entry gates below are tightened at the same time. Do not adopt the spot bias without the gates.

bidAskDownsidePctYoung 90 -> 72 and Mature 65 -> 60 (handoff band 70-75). This does NOT create bins above (see SDK constraint) — it concentrates the below-range so fee density near the active bin is higher instead of smeared across a 90% price drop.

Entry gates tightened for tail suppression, all implicated in the 7 tail losses (3 of which were instant dumps: -57% in 6min, -33% in 2min, -25% in 0min): athEntryGateEnabled ON (handoff requirement), minTvl 6000->20000, maxTop10Pct 50->32, rugcheckTop10MaxPct 100->35 (100 = effectively disabled), maxBotHoldersPct 35->25, maxBundlerTop100Pct 25->20, minTokenAgeHours 4->12, minTokenFeesSol 8->12, autoStrategyMaxPumpPct1h 15->12, autoStrategyMaxOorRisk 50->40.

security.concentrationParadoxOverrideEnabled true -> false for this phase. It lets smart-money presence override concentration limits; while we are explicitly tightening maxTop10Pct to suppress concentration-driven rugs, leaving an override on undercuts the whole change.

darwinEnabled true -> false. Signal weights re-evolving every 5 closes would confound evaluation of this preset. filterAutotuneEnabled and autoRecovery also stay off. No self-modification during the evaluation window.

minAgeBeforeYieldCheck deliberately KEPT at 60 and minFeePerTvl24h at 2.5. LOW_YIELD is the largest exit class (51) but is expectancy-NEUTRAL ex-tail (+0.011%) — it is correctly culling dead pools and recycling the single position slot. Also note daemon/engine/close-rules.js rule 5 HARDCODES the age gate to >= 60, ignoring minAgeBeforeYieldCheck, so changing this key would silently do nothing in the daemon. See RR_V1_REDESIGN.md follow-ups.
severeLossPct 10 -> 8 so the 72h cooldown + 50% size cap engage just past the new -6% stop / -9% backstop band instead of well beyond it. lossRedeployCooldownHours 8 -> 12.
dailyLossLimitUsd 28 -> 18 (handoff band 15-20). At ~$75/SOL a 0.5 SOL position is ~$37, so a -6% stop is ~-$2.2 and 18 allows ~8 stops before the day halts.

NOT changed and worth a later look: minFeeActiveTvlRatio stays 0.1 (tightening it risks starving the screener to zero candidates — revisit after dry-run candidate flow is confirmed); partialTpEnabled stays off (a $37 position leaves dust); noDeployAfterHour stays null.
Run `node scripts/apply-preset.js garda-rr-v1 --dry-run` to review the exact diff before applying.
